page: Microsoft Azure E4ps_v5 is a memory-optimized virtual machine belonging to the EPSv5 server family, running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features an arm64 architecture with 4 dedicated physical cores and 4 vCPUs utilizing the 3.0 GHz Ampere Altra ARMv8 Neoverse-N1 processor. The system is equipped with 32.0 GB of RAM, yielding a resource density of 8.0 GB of memory per core. It contains no local storage, though it is Premium Storage capable, and does not include any GPUs or complimentary public IPv4 addresses.

Benchmark data indicates average performance in several key areas, alongside notable limitations. The single-core and multi-core stress-ng CPU tests scored 1822.69 and 7249.86 respectively, placing them in the average tier. Large block memory bandwidth read and write speeds also performed in the average range at 50.14 GB/sec and 29.77 GB/sec. However, the server exhibits weak performance in Geekbench single-core (1122.0) and multi-core (3707.0) metrics, as well as in software compilation and image processing. Cryptographic capabilities are a significant bottleneck, with the Passmark CPU encryption test registering a poor score of 652.89, and LLM inference speeds for a small 135M model are also poor, reaching only 24.0 tokens/sec for text generation.

From a qualitative cost-efficiency perspective, the E4ps_v5 offers a high memory-to-vCPU ratio on an ARM-based architecture, which typically translates to lower operational costs compared to x86 equivalents with similar memory footprints. However, the trade-off lies in its lower raw compute and cryptographic performance. This profile makes the server suitable for memory-intensive workloads that do not require heavy computational or cryptographic processing, such as database operations, caching layers, and general memory-optimized web applications.
